one_month_reasoning: No Micron earnings before 1 Nov (FQ1 FY27 report mid/late Dec). In the window: (1) Taiwan union strike vote (early Oct) and Taichung mediation on 22 Oct over a 15%-of-operating-profit bonus demand [17], a negative-skew headline (a stoppage would actually tighten supply, so the fundamental hit is ambiguous); (2) Netlist's second ITC complaint, filed ~27-29 Sep against Micron HBM3E/HBM4/HBM4E with Nvidia, Google and Broadcom as respondents [14,15]; the ITC normally votes on institution about 30 days after filing, so a late-Oct institution headline is likely, which is noise rather than value (Samsung settled with Netlist in Aug-26; an exclusion order would be 15+ months away); (3) Samsung Q3 prelim (~7-8 Oct) and full results, SK hynix Q3 (27/28 Oct), FOMC (27-28 Oct), hyperscaler Q3 capex guides; spot DRAM is flat and CSPs are still buying server DRAM [24], so the peer prints should read supportive. The stock moved only +0.9% across a guide ~8% above consensus, which says positioning is full. Net: a near-symmetric lognormal centred slightly below spot (~$1,066) with ~21% one-month sigma (80%/3.5 = 23%, trimmed as part of realized vol came from the 5x run-up).

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of (a) FY28 EPS $195 (5% below $206 consensus) x 5.0x horizon P/E = $975 and (b) a cycle-aware DCF to Oct-2027 (FY28-31 FCF/share $148/$100/$35/$30, terminal $55 mid-cycle EPS x 12, 11% discount) of $702 plus ~$175/share net cash = $877. Blend ~$925, ~14% below spot.

inputs_detail.value: Yahoo $176.42 vs MarketBeat quarterly sum ~$189; FQ1 guide $38.15 ~8% above pre-print consensus
inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus is more likely to rise than fall after the guide beat.

Consensus $205.95 less ~5% (was 10%). Kept a small haircut for HBM content cuts (12-high to 8-high) [21,22], +$2.5B FY27 opex and 'more moderate' price increases [2], and slowing hyperscaler capex growth [20]; narrowed from 10% because the guide beat and the higher MarketBeat FY27 sum argue against a deep cut, and management (primary) expects the industry supply constrained in both CY27 and CY28.

inputs_detail.input: Horizon P/E multiple (on FY28 = NTM at Oct-27)
inputs_detail.derivation: Core memory peers on an NTM basis: SK hynix ~4.65x, Samsung ~4.73x, Kioxia ~4.2x, Nanya ~5.4x, Sandisk ~7.8x; median ~4.7x. MU trades ~6.0x NTM today, and historically at mid-single-digit P/E at peaks [23]. 5.0x is ~6% over the median for SCA floors (>35% of revenue to 2030, $150B RPO at minimum prices) [2]; below the 5.2x supervisor cap because SK hynix/Samsung also have long-term contracts and the market will be pricing FY28 as a peak with supply additions visible.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Value at Oct-27 = PV(FCF/share FY28 $148, FY29 $100, FY30 $35, FY31 $30) $263 + PV(terminal $55 x 12 = $660) $439 at 11% = $702; plus net cash ~$175/share = $877

inputs_detail.derivation: $195 EPS + ~$13 D&A/share (FY26 D&A $9.5B rising with capex) - ~$60 capex/share (~$69B FY28 capex: FY27 >$50B with $25B in 1H and 2H higher, construction capex growing faster) on ~1.15B diluted shares [1,2].

Management expects supply constrained through CY28 [2], so FY29 (Sep-28 to Aug-29) still has a tight first half (raised from $75). The downturn is placed in FY30-31 as dated cleanroom additions ramp: Micron ID1 and Tongluo mid-27, ID2 and Japan late-28, Singapore NAND 2H28 [2]; SK hynix Y1 Feb-27 and Samsung P5 1H27 [18]; CXMT 420k wpm [19]. Capex cut to $35-40B in the trough; peak-cycle history [23].

Mid-cycle EPS ~$55 (~$63B NI) reflects structurally higher HBM/data-center mix and SCA floors, where management says margins at floor prices are above prior cycle peaks [2]; 12x mid-cycle P/E consistent with mid-single-digit at peaks and higher at mid-cycle [23].
High-beta cyclical (80% realized vol per brief); BBB+ at all three agencies with $5.2B debt [2], so cost of capital ~ cost of equity ~11%.

inputs_detail.input: Net cash per share at Oct-27
inputs_detail.derivation: $68.3B net cash less $12.7B refundable SCA deposits = $55.6B, plus ~$145-150B FY27 FCF (consensus NI ~$203B + ~$12B D&A - ~$55B+ capex) = ~$200B / 1.15B diluted shares; buybacks value-neutral. Confirmed by supervisor recomputation.

bear.story: By mid-2027 the market looks through the shortage as dated supply lands (SK hynix Y1 Feb-27, Samsung P5 1H27, Micron ID1 and Tongluo mid-27, CXMT 420k wpm), hyperscaler capex growth slows (UBS +25% 2027, +6% 2028) and GPU makers cut HBM content (8-high). FY28 consensus is cut toward $130 and the stock trades ~4.5x that (~$585), consistent with MU's 50-70% peak-cycle drawdowns. Probability cut from 32% because management's primary guidance has supply constrained through CY28 and the sentiment sources I leaned on (Burry stock short, Polymarket, KuCoin) were stale or weak.

base.story: FY27 delivers at or above consensus (~$180-190) and FY28 ~$195-205, but by Oct-27 investors treat FY28 as the peak; the multiple settles near the ~4.7-5.0x memory-peer range while ~$175/sh of cash builds. Stock roughly flat to slightly down.

bull.story: Shortage proves structural (management has no line of sight to balance and sees CY27-28 much tighter than 2026), HBM 2027 resets +70-140%, FY28 EPS $230+, capital return steps up from 9 Dec 2026 and the market pays 7x+ for SCA-backed earnings plus cash.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A small premium only, for documented contractual features that persist through the horizon: 26 SCAs at >35% of revenue through 2030, $150B RPO at minimum prices and $32B customer commitments, with floor-price margins above prior cycle peaks [2]. Capped below the supervisor's 5.2x because SK hynix and Samsung also hold long-term HBM/DRAM contracts and large net cash, and SCA ceilings cap upside capture. No premium for US listing or sell-side outperform calls.

thesis_break_reason: Rebuilt from post-print inputs: $615 (-43%) is ~4.7x (the core memory NTM median) on FY28 EPS of ~$130, i.e. the market capitalising a ~35% cut to $206 consensus, or ~2.1x consensus FY28 ex the ~$175/sh projected net cash. That cut is only consistent with outright contract-price declines in 2027 or SCA floors being renegotiated, against management's primary guidance of supply constrained through CY28 [2]. Trading there would mean the cycle turned a year earlier than my base case (my bear case confirmed), not ordinary multiple compression.

reasoning: Round 2. Facts unchanged from round 1 and confirmed by the supervisor against the 8-K and prepared remarks: FQ4 $54.2B/$33.42, FQ1 guide $61.5B/$38.15 (~8% above consensus), net cash $68.3B, $12.7B deposits, $150B RPO [1,2]. What changed: (1) Multiple: on a clean NTM basis the core memory median is ~4.7x, not 5.1x (my round-1 median included HDD/controller names), so I cut 5.5x to 5.0x. (2) FY28 EPS: haircut narrowed from 10% to 5% ($195) given the guide beat and MarketBeat FY27 ~$189 vs Yahoo $176 [4]. (3) Re-reading the prepared remarks myself: management expects supply 'much tighter in CY27 and CY28' and the industry constrained in both years, with ID2/Japan/Singapore NAND only in late-28 [2]; I moved the DCF downturn one year later (FY29 FCF $75->$100), which lifts the DCF from $843 to $877. The P/E and DCF changes net out, so fair value moves only $930->$925, still ~14% below spot. (4) Skeptic evidence re-weighted: Burry swapped his stock short for June-2027 ~$500 puts on 28 Sep [7]; I read that as a more leveraged but time-limited bet that needs a >50% fall by June, which I put at well under 10%, so it is sentiment and does not move numbers; Polymarket snippets and the KuCoin blog are dropped; Morningstar is kept as sentiment only. Credit is not a risk: BBB+ at all three agencies, $5.2B debt [2]. New in-lane find: Netlist filed a second ITC complaint ~27-29 Sep targeting Micron HBM3E/HBM4/HBM4E with Nvidia, Google and Broadcom as respondents [14,15]; with a prior $445M verdict [16] and Samsung's Aug-26 settlement, a low-single-digit-$B settlement is the likely path, immaterial to ~$200B of FY27 FCF, while an exclusion order is a tail. Spot DRAM is flat with CSPs still buying [24], so there is no near-term price crack. (5) Scenarios: bear $580 (27%, from 32%, tied to dated supply additions rather than sentiment), base $1,000 (48%), bull $1,700 (25%); expected ~$1,060, median ~$1,000. Ladder is a three-lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.35/0.25/0.25) with a fattened far left tail, giving P(>=1075) 0.44 (from 0.42) and P(<537) ~11.5%. I stay below the supervisor's ladder because my fair value is lower and I weight the 2027 discounting of the 2028 supply wave more heavily. Thesis break rebuilt to $615 from post-print FY28 inputs. Research limits: about 8 follow-up queries; one French Netlist article returned 403.
